messages.subject: Compare.evol.rates and univariate data
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to use the compare.evol.rates function with univariate data (centroid size) and I am running into an issue.

Following the vignettes and Dr. Sherratt's "Guide to Geomorph", I transformed the data into a matrix with rownames giving taxa names. However, I get the following error:

Error in if (N != dim(x)[1]) { : argument is of length zero

Here is the same behavior, recreated using the plethspecies dataset.

data(plethspecies) 
Y.gpa<-gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment    
gp.end<-factor(c(0,0,1,0,0,1,1,0,0))  #endangered species vs. rest
names(gp.end)<-plethspecies$phy$tip

#Compare evol rates
ER.shape <- compare.evol.rates(A=Y.gpa$coords,phy=plethspecies$phy, gp=gp.end ,iter=999) #This works!
summary(ER.shape)

Csize <- matrix(Y.gpa$Csize, dimnames=list(names(Y.gpa$Csize))) # make matrix

ER.size <- compare.evol.rates(A=Y.gpa$Csize,phy=plethspecies$phy, gp=gp.end ,iter=999) #This does not work!
Error in if (N != dim(x)[1]) { : argument is of length zero

Could someone point out what I am doing wrong?

Thank you,
Tony

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Compare.evol.rates and univariate data
parts:
Do not follow that guide; it is very out of date.

 

If you take the example directly from the help file of the function and change the last line to point to Y.gpa$Csize, it works just fine.

 

ER<-compare.evol.rates(A=Y.gpa$Csize, phy=plethspecies$phy,method="simulation",gp=gp.end,iter=999)

 

Dean

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Compare.evol.rates and univariate data
parts: Not your PC but likely your version of base-R, geomorph, and RRPP.  Earlier this fall R went to R 4.0, then 4.0.1 and 4.0.2. There were major changes to how various data structures are now handled, which caused cascading effects in many packages including geomorph and RRPP.  We’ve updated to accommodate, but this usually requires a fresh install of everything to sort out (at least, that seems to have solved similar issues that others have had: see prior threads on this list).

Dean
